rival_explanations: A formal/academic-register neuron: the pole tracks the vocabulary of written academic, clinical and institutional prose (cross-reference words, figure and section labels, demographic and clinical nouns, past participles of inquiry) rather than a fixed token list, so unseen formal content words such as 'methodology', 'hypothesis', 'regression', 'pursuant' and 'wherein' should fire - all measure 0.00.

A relational/degree-marker neuron: the pole encodes relative position and comparison ('above', 'over', 'beyond', 'below', 'equal', 'larger', 'smaller', 'further'), so other position and comparison markers such as 'higher', 'lower', 'under', 'beneath', 'between' and 'across' should fire - they measure 0.07, 0.00, 0.06, 0.04, 0.00 and 0.00, while 'cancer', 'FIG', 'surveyed' and ' gender' fire with no relational content.

A rare-final-piece neuron: it fires whenever a word's last BPE piece is an uncommon fragment, so firing should follow the tokenizer and word rarity rather than a token list - yet 2.4% of single-piece words fire (' FIG' 0.66, ' cancer' 0.48, ' male' 0.43 are single tokens) and the common final pieces 'ology', 'tion', 'ment', 'ing', 'ed', 'ly', 'al', 'ic', 'ent', 'ant' and 'ure' all measure 0.00.

Lady Gaga x Terry Richardson

Lady Gaga x Terry Richardson is a photo-book by American singer Lady Gaga and American photographer Terry Richardson, released on November 22, 2011 by Grand Central Publishing. The book features more than 350 pictures of Gaga as taken by Richardson during a ten-month period from Gaga's performance at The Monster Ball Tour till the 2011 Grammy Awards. In addition to photographs, it includes a foreword written by the singer about her relationship with Richardson. The duo had collaborated on other projects prior to the shooting of the book.

Upon release, Lady Gaga x Terry Richardson received positive reviews from critics, who praised both the provocative pictures as well as simpler shots of Gaga without makeup and stage costumes. The book appeared at number five on The New York Times Best Seller list, before fluctuating down the ranking in subsequent weeks. Due to a lawsuit against Gaga by her former assistant, in 2013 the photos taken by Richardson were asked to be submitted as evidence for the case.

Background and inspiration

Lady Gaga x Terry Richardson consists of photos (in black-and-white and in color) that Richardson took of Gaga during a ten-month period, ranging from the singer's performance at Lollapalooza in 2010 to the final shows of her 2009 – 11 Monster Ball Tour. More than 100,000 pictures were taken during the time period with over 350 appearing in the book. The book also includes a Gaga-written foreword about her relationship with Richardson that doubles as an examination of self. "With Terry, the relationship extends beyond the photograph, and if you're lucky, he will teach you something truly profound about yourself."

Prior to the shooting of Lady Gaga x Terry Richardson, Gaga and Richardson had worked together on several project. These include an advertisement for New York skate shop and clothing brand Supreme and photoshoots for Vogue Hommes Japan and Harper's Bazaar. Jamie Raab (executive vice president of Grand Central Publishing) said "We are proud to be publishing this remarkable collaboration between Lady Gaga and Terry Richardson and anticipate that it will be one of the most stunning, provocative and coveted books of the 2011 holiday season."

Gaga claimed that she held nothing back from Richardson, who was with her "every minute, every moment" during the photographing period. She explained that the images were completely unfiltered and he shot her waking up in the morning, doing her chores, as well as images taken while she got ready in her bathroom. She added that true to Richardson's photographing style, nothing in the book was staged and he was able to make her do things in front of the camera that has not been done by anyone previously. Richardson also took pictures of Gaga's fans for the book – which she appreciated – explaining to The Hollywood Reporter:

"My favorite thing, honestly, is that [Richardson] loved the fans. He shot the fans the same way he shot me: with no pretense. N

Step-by-Step Guide to Beginning a Daily Journaling Practice

Journaling is a therapeutic and introspective process that can lead to self-discovery and personal growth. With consistency, you can establish a journaling habit that becomes a significant part of your routine. Follow these steps to start your daily journaling practice:

Step 1: Choose a Journal

Select a journal that makes you excited to write. It can be a notebook, a binder, or a digital document. Choose one that is easy to carry around and has ample space for your writing.

Step 2: Choose a Time and Place

Set up a consistent time and place to journal. Choose a space that is private, calm, and free from distractions. It can be anywhere from your bed to a quiet corner in your living room.

Step 3: Decide on a Frequency

Decide on how often you want to write. It can be daily, weekly, or monthly, as long as it is consistent. Doing it daily will help you develop a habit and stay committed to your practice.

Step 4: Set a Goal

Come up with an intention or goal for your writing. Ask yourself what you want to achieve by journaling. Do you want to clarify your thoughts, reduce stress, or track progress toward a specific goal?

Step 5: Choose a Writing Style

Select a writing style that suits you. You can choose between reflective, creative, or factual journaling. Reflective journaling involves recording thoughts and feelings, while creative journaling involves illustrating thoughts and ideas. Factual journaling involves recording events in your life.

Step 6: Choose What to Write About

Start by choosing a prompt or topic for your journal entry. A topic can be anything that comes to your mind. It can be something that happened during the day or a significant memory. Explore your emotions and thoughts about the topic.

Step 7: Write Down Your Thoughts

Write down your thoughts and feelings without judgment. Don't worry about grammar, spelling, or punctuation. Write freely and honestly. Allow your thoughts to flow naturally, and don't overthink what you're writing.

Step 8: Reflect on Your Writing

Reflect on what you've written and how it made you feel. Identify any patterns, triggers or insights. Writing down your thoughts helps you connect with your emotions, goals, and aspirations. Use journaling as an opportunity to explore your inner self.

Tips for Successful Journaling

- Be consistent with your practice. Write regularly, and choose a specific time and place to journal.
- Use prompts to help you get started, but don't feel constrained by them.
- Write freely and honestly. Don't worry about what others will think or how it might appear to someone else.
- Reflect on your writing and use it as a tool for self-discovery and personal growth.

## What you need to know

### Pressure Force Area

Area is a measure of the size of a surface and is usually measured in square metres. Force is a measure of how much push or pull is being exerted onto an object and is usually measured in Newtons (N). Pressure is a measure of how much force is applied over a given area of an object, so it is calculated by dividing the amount of force being applied by the area over which its being applied.

The units we used to measure pressure are compound units (for more information, see here (https://mathsmadeeasy.co.uk/gcse-maths-revision/conversions-gcse-revision-and-worksheets/)). Another useful topic to revise is rearranging formulae

readings.explanation: Retrospective, context-free per-BPE-token lookup at layer 0: the pole's strength is a fixed function of the single current token, so the same token gives the same value in every context, language and position (a sweep of all 50,254 token ids reproduces every scan value, and input attribution puts 100% of the peak on that token and 0% on the previous one), and a text fires iff at least one of its tokens after the first is in the pole's fixed active set. 'above' dominates that set: bare 'above' 1.11 x max (the value seen inside brackets), ' above' 1.02, ' Above' 0.62, and the word's sense is irrelevant - physical height ('The chart above is wrong.' 1.02) and document back-reference ('the tools above' 1.02) fire identically; 'ABOVE' cannot fire whole because the tokenizer splits it into ' AB'+'OVE' (0.31). The rest of the set is a fixed, semantically heterogeneous slice of about 1,900 of the 50,254 BPE tokens (3.8% of the vocabulary, 1.7% of running prose) that has to be named as tokens rather than as a class, because near-synonyms split badly. A relational/degree-marker neuron: the pole encodes relative position and comparison ('above', 'over', 'beyond', 'below', 'equal', 'larger', 'smaller', 'further'), so other position and comparison markers such as 'higher', 'lower', 'under', 'beneath', 'between' and 'across' should fire - they measure 0.07, 0.00, 0.06, 0.04, 0.00 and 0.00, while 'cancer', 'FIG', 'surveyed' and ' gender' fire with no relational content.

A rare-final-piece neuron: it fires whenever a word's last BPE piece is an uncommon fragment, so firing should follow the tokenizer and word rarity rather than a token list - yet 2.4% of single-piece words fire (' FIG' 0.66, ' cancer' 0.48, ' male' 0.43 are single tokens) and the common final pieces 'ology', 'tion', 'ment', 'ing', 'ed', 'ly', 'al', 'ic', 'ent', 'ant' and 'ure' all measure 0.00.
